name: Candidates in the order the production rules give
purpose: The work that competes for attention comes back in the order the systems that carry it state for it.
record: Cases from the ordering rules Quest and Quest AI Runner state in their own code and tests (quest list rank, autopilot work order, goal ladder, open asks), some using the tests' own data and the rest written to exercise a stated rule; one number: the share of cases whose whole order equals the reviewed order, balanced with cost and time by [balance.prioritization], weights and budgets fixed before any arm was scored. Mean pairwise agreement is in the details.
disadvantages: Few cases from one production system's rules. No repository holds real examples of a person's explicit order, deferral, feedback or not-before constraints, so those are covered by unit tests, not by this number; weights derived from implied priorities are not yet compared with what a person confirms.
cascading_conditionals: free [sample=full | real=no | gate=competitive | when=the arm and its rivals were recorded on the same cases]
command: esoi run prioritization --impl stated_fields; esoi run prioritization --impl as_given
